zh: 但事实是，根本没有什么接近共同主线的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone does it differently, and there is no playbook.
zh: 每个人的做法都不一样，根本没有什么手册。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the playbooks are changing extra fast right now.
zh: 而且这些手册现在变化得特别快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my last two interviews are emblematic of it.
zh: 我最近两次采访就是典型的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I interviewed Tarek from Kalshi.
zh: 我采访了 Kalshi 的 Tarek。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he and his co-founder have, I forget, 200 employees.
zh: 他和他的联合创始人有——我记不清了——200 名员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no levels of management.
zh: 没有管理层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all report to those two.
zh: 所有人都向他们两个人汇报。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he referred to it in the podcast as management by chaos.
zh: 他在播客里把这称为“混沌管理”。

speaker: Unknown
en: My last interview was with Aliotze from Databricks, and he's got eight direct reports.
zh: 我最近一次采访的是 Databricks 的 Aliotze，他有 8 个直接下属。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's, you know, very structured.
zh: 就是，你知道的，非常有结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: His direct report team, he has three meetings a week with his direct reports.
zh: 他的直接下属团队，他每周和直接下属开三次会。

speaker: Unknown
en: He has a QBR.
zh: 他有一个 QBR（季度业务回顾）。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once a quarter, and then he has an off-site strategy session once a quarter.
zh: 每季度一次，然后他每季度还有一次线下战略会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: So polar opposites both doing extremely well.
zh: 所以是完全相反的两个极端，但都做得极其出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you fit in that spectrum?
zh: 你在这个光谱中处于什么位置？

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably somewhere in between.
zh: 大概介于两者之间吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think these things are generally more formal approaches to management.
zh: 我觉得这些通常是比较正式的管理方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're greatly overestimated in the impact.
zh: 我觉得它们的影响被大大高估了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a company's outcome, I think almost all of the outcome depends on essentially your strategy, what people sometimes call product-market fit, but also the modes you have.
zh: 对一家公司的结果而言，我认为几乎所有结果本质上取决于你的战略，也就是人们有时说的产品市场契合度，还有你拥有的护城河。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's overwhelmingly what drives it.
zh: 这才是压倒性地起决定作用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always ask myself, to me, a business is a good business if it would do well even if management was mediocre, maybe not awful, but mediocre.
zh: 我总是问自己，对我而言，一家企业是好企业的标准是，即便管理层平庸它也能表现良好——也许不是糟糕，但平庸。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the first thing.
zh: 这是第一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second thing that matters to me is talent levels some culture.
zh: 而对我重要的第二点是人才水平和某种文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which culture is really like, you know, how do you make decisions?
zh: 所谓文化其实就是，你知道的，你如何做决策？

speaker: Unknown
en: What matters?
zh: 什么重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: What doesn't?
zh: 什么不重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we value?
zh: 我们重视什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we not value?
zh: 我们不重视什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Then everything else, you know, reporting lines, whether you have OKRs or you keep it fluid and informal span of control.
zh: 然后其他所有东西，你知道的，汇报关系线，你是用 OKR 还是保持灵活非正式的管理幅度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure it does matter on the margin, you know, making things a bit better, a bit worse.
zh: 我确信在边际上它确实有影响，你知道的，能让事情好一点或差一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm sure different solutions would be optimal depending on the people involved, because ultimately a manager, a CEO is
zh: 而且我确信不同的方案会因涉及的人不同而各有其最优解，因为归根结底一个管理者、一个 CEO 是

speaker: Unknown
en: Some sort of a leader or should be.
zh: 某种领导者，或者应该是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the same strategy, the same approach to working with others depends on the human capital you have.
zh: 同样的战略、同样的与他人协作的方式，取决于你所拥有的人力资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Different people react different.
zh: 不同的人反应不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: The culture you're trying to foster.
zh: 还有你试图培育的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that within reason, that doesn't make a huge difference.
zh: 但我认为在合理范围内，这不会造成巨大差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe like a plus minus 10%.
zh: 大概正负 10% 左右吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think you're much better off obsessing over, first and foremost, a strategy, but then once that's in place, the quality of the people and the culture you establish.
zh: 所以我认为你最好是痴迷于——首先是战略，然后一旦战略就位，就是人员的质量和你所建立的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if the 200% organization chaotic, super high, I don't know them, but assuming, super high talent density, a culture of business orientation, rationality, hard work.
zh: 所以如果这家组织有 200% 的混乱、超高……我不了解他们，但假设，超高的人才密度，一种业务导向、理性、努力工作的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if a little extra structure theoretically could be helpful, I think the talent and the culture will mostly trump any such gap or close any such gap and vice versa.
zh: 即使理论上多一点结构可能会有帮助，我认为人才和文化大体上会胜过、弥补任何这样的差距，反之亦然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe in the other extreme, a little bit more fluidity and flexibility would be ideal, but if you have very good people and a great culture, let's get it done for the benefit of the business, people will not get stuck because there is a little extra structure.
zh: 也许在另一个极端，多一点流动性和灵活性会更理想，但如果你有很好的人、很棒的文化，为了业务利益把事情做成，人们不会因为多一点结构而卡住。

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't thought a lot about these things.
zh: 我没有太多思考过这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm convinced they're not the most important thing, to be honest, in excelling in business.
zh: 老实说，我相信它们不是在商业上出类拔萃的最重要因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fascinating.
zh: 有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I was the CEO, I tried to get better and evolve as the business scaled, and I got a lot of feedback.
zh: 我当 CEO 的时候，随着业务扩张，我努力变得更好、不断进化，我收到了很多反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the pieces of feedback I got a couple of times was, Brian, you're a very good leader and a very bad manager.
zh: 其中有一条我收到了好几次的反馈是：Brian,你是一个非常好的领导者，也是一个非常糟糕的管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are you on that?
zh: 你在这上面处于什么位置?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get a lot of feedback.
zh: 我收到很多反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think anyone kind of rated me on those two, against those two archetypes or job descriptions.
zh: 我不觉得有人真的按照这两个原型或职位描述给我打过分。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think?
zh: 你怎么看?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll put a little self-reflection here.
zh: 我在这里做一点自我反思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think, yeah, I'm not sure if I'm a good leader or a good manager, to be honest.
zh: 我不觉得，嗯，说实话，我不确定自己是一个好的领导者还是一个好的管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I generally feel that
zh: 我总体上觉得

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm pretty privileged that I work with very good people and I tend to be more self-conscious and question whether I'm doing enough and I'm living up to expectations.
zh: 我很幸运能和很好的人共事，而我往往更自觉，会质疑自己是否做得足够、是否达到了期望。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I tend to see the glass half empty.
zh: 所以我往往把杯子看成半空的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So my instinctual reaction would be I'm probably not terrible at either.
zh: 所以我的本能反应会是，我在这两方面大概都不算糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would be disingenuous if I told you I think I suck.
zh: 如果我告诉你我觉得自己很烂，那是不真诚的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I would probably rate myself something like
zh: 但我大概会给自己打一个类似这样的分：

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay at both, but not necessarily amazing.
zh: 两方面都还行，但不一定出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm probably a better leader than manager if I understand what you're hinting at.
zh: 如果我理解你暗示的意思，我作为领导者大概比作为管理者更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I've generally done okay at setting a vision that made sense and a compelling vision and communicating that reasonably well.
zh: 我认为我总体上在设定一个合理的愿景、一个有吸引力的愿景，并且把它传达得还不错这方面，做得还行。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I've succeeded as a leader as being mostly through what I would call servant leadership, like just working super hard and helping people as much as I could, I don't think I'm the kind of William Wallace kind of leader, someone making a grand speech and everybody gets their hearts pounding and everybody gets to work.
zh: 如果说我作为领导者取得过成功，那主要是通过我所谓的仆人式领导，就是超级努力地工作，尽我所能地帮助别人。我不觉得我是那种 William Wallace 式的领导者——发表一番宏大的演讲，让每个人都热血沸腾、每个人都去干活。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you work with someone who walks the talk and
zh: 但当你和一个言行一致的人共事时，

speaker: Unknown
en: Is in the trenches and does their best.
zh: 一个身处第一线、竭尽全力的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you tend to be inspired.
zh: 我觉得你往往会受到鼓舞。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe that kind of person.
zh: 所以也许就是那种人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I try to be that kind of person.
zh: 我努力成为那种人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I'm a great manager.
zh: 我不觉得自己是一个出色的管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I'm the best at running one-on-ones or anything like that.
zh: 我不觉得自己擅长开一对一或类似的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things I used to say to myself is actually, I got this quote from Eleanor Roosevelt of all people.
zh: 我过去常对自己说的一句话，其实是，我从 Eleanor Roosevelt 那里得到的一句话，竟然是她。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to keep my head in the clouds, but my feet on the ground.
zh: 我想让我的头在云端，但我的脚在地上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And
zh: 而且

speaker: Unknown
en: By that, I meant I wanted to be, okay, a JV, William Wallace, painting a picture of the future, getting everyone excited about where we're going, looking over their horizon.
zh: 我的意思是，我想成为，好吧，一个 JV 版的 William Wallace,描绘未来的图景，让每个人对我们要去的地方感到兴奋，眺望地平线。

speaker: Unknown
en: But being in the ground, it's like, holy crap, there are a lot of problems, and we have to deal with all these freaking problems.
zh: 但同时脚踏实地，就是，天哪，有好多问题，我们得处理所有这些该死的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my glass was very half empty, and I spent a lot of times a little negative looking at the problems.
zh: 而且我的杯子非常半空，我花了很多时间带着一点消极的态度去看这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are you in the Eleanor Roosevelt quote?
zh: 你在这句 Eleanor Roosevelt 的话里处于什么位置?

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to give myself a little pat on the shoulder.
zh: 我想给自己一点肯定。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if there's one thing I tend to do reasonably well is
zh: 我觉得如果说有一件事我做得还算不错，那就是

speaker: Unknown
en: Being able to see the big picture, so I guess head in the cloud kind of thing.
zh: 能够看到大局，所以我猜算是头在云端那类。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I'm not the best at, say, articulating it again with the grand speech, but I think I'm pretty good in the substance at understanding what matters, what doesn't, where the opportunity is, what logically we should be doing, and what's just noise.
zh: 也许我不太擅长，比如说，再强调一下，用宏大的演讲把它表达出来，但我觉得我在实质内容上相当不错，能理解什么重要、什么不重要、机会在哪里、逻辑上我们应该做什么、什么只是噪音。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think I've historically been very hands-on in the details, in the trenches.
zh: 而且我认为我在细节上历来是非常亲力亲为的，身处第一线。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a good quality that you want to have as an entrepreneur and CEO.
zh: 我认为这是作为一个创业者和 CEO 你想拥有的一个好品质。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not super widespread in the population, but it's quite commonly found, I think, in entrepreneurs and CEOs.
zh: 它在普通人群中并不算特别普遍，但我认为在创业者和 CEO 中相当常见。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's quite powerful because if you don't have the big picture, you can't really set a directional strategy that's the winning strategy unless someone else brings it to you, which is always nice, but you can't count on that happening.
zh: 而且我认为它非常有力，因为如果你没有大局观，你就无法真正制定一个作为制胜策略的方向性战略，除非别人把它带给你——那当然很好，但你不能指望那种事发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hope is not a strategy, as they say.
zh: 正如人们所说，希望不是一种策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're not in the details, in the trenches, feet firmly planted on the ground, then I think you're unlikely to be able to inform that big picture properly.
zh: 但如果你不在细节中、不在第一线、没有把脚牢牢踩在地上，那么我认为你不太可能正确地校准那个大局。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're unlikely to be inspiring to your colleagues.
zh: 你不太可能对你的同事有激励作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very few people like working with people who are in an ivory tower.
zh: 很少有人喜欢和身处象牙塔里的人一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't get their hands dirty.
zh: 他们不亲自动手。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't really scale.
zh: 这真的无法规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's not...
zh: 我觉得这并不……

speaker: Unknown
en: Good.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not in a position to assess others, to coach others, because you don't really know anything about the work at some point.
zh: 你没有资格评估别人、指导别人，因为到了某个时候，你对这份工作其实一无所知。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do believe you need both to be successful.
zh: 所以我确实认为，要取得成功，两者你都需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, finding some sort of equilibrium.
zh: 而且，你知道，要找到某种平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: I find it's easier to sequence those activities and trying to run them in parallel.
zh: 我发现把这些活动按先后顺序安排，比试图同时并行进行要容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I try to have times where I'm very much in the clouds thinking, okay, what are the big problems and big opportunities?
zh: 所以我会有一段时间完全在云端思考：好，最大的问题和最大的机会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How should you go about them and be more of an architect?
zh: 你应该如何着手处理它们，更多地扮演一个架构师的角色？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then long stretches where I just get into execution mode and I'm, you know, mad...
zh: 然后是很长一段时间的纯粹执行模式，我，你知道，疯狂地……

speaker: Unknown
en: Head to toe, just getting stuff done, you know, blood, sweat and tears.
zh: 从头到脚，就是把事情做完，你知道，流血、流汗、流泪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's quite difficult to be both at the same time, but you can be both in sequence.
zh: 我觉得同时兼顾两者相当困难，但你可以按先后顺序做到两者兼顾。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's talk about coaching for a second.
zh: 我们来聊一下指导(coaching)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Similar to me, I had never been CEO of a company with thousands of employees in public, and I was figuring out as I went along.
zh: 和我类似，我从来没有在公开市场上管理过一家有数千名员工的公司，我是一边做一边摸索的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes I just didn't feel qualified to coach some of my executives.
zh: 有时我就是觉得自己不够格去指导我的一些高管。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you ever have that feeling?
zh: 你有过那种感觉吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And also related to that, so many of the CEOs I'm working with, like,
zh: 还有与此相关的是，我合作的很多 CEO 都是，

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a very talented person internally.
zh: 他们内部有一个非常有才华的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're on their way up.
zh: 这个人正在上升期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Should they bet on that person or find someone who's seen the movie before and has a little bit of experience?
zh: 他们应该押注这个人，还是找一个之前看过这部电影、有一些经验的人？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's happening everywhere across Silicon Valley right now.
zh: 就像现在整个硅谷到处都在发生这种事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we hire to bet on that person or should we make the person, bet on the person who's on their way up and really hasn't seen anything close to this movie?
zh: 我们是该招人来押注那个人，还是该押注那个正在上升期、但真的还没看过任何接近这部电影的人？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, on coaching, I'm certainly inadequate as a coach often with people I work with.
zh: 那么，关于指导，和我共事的一些人面前，我作为教练当然常常是不称职的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think at Bend In Spoons we work off the assumption that our managers
zh: 我不认为在 Bend In Spoons 我们是基于这样一种假设来运作的，即我们的管理者

speaker: Unknown
en: should always be capable of solving or advising on a solution across all problems that are experienced by direct reports.
zh: 应该始终有能力为直接下属遇到的所有问题解决或提供解决方案建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just think that any one person may be able to coach any other person on some things, and they should do so regardless of reporting lines.
zh: 我们只是认为，任何一个人都可以在某些事情上指导其他任何一个人，而且无论汇报关系如何，他们都应该这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a good manager would generally be someone very smart, a good problem solver, so at least they can provide generalist support.
zh: 我认为一个好的管理者通常是一个非常聪明的人、一个好的问题解决者，这样至少他们能提供通才式的支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: They should be emotionally supported and ready to get their hands dirty, but ultimately, being someone's manager doesn't mean you're always in a better position to solve a problem for them.
zh: 他们应该提供情感上的支持，并准备好亲自动手，但归根结底，做某个人的管理者并不意味着你总是处于更有利的位置去为他们解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are so many skills needed in a business like yours, like ours.
zh: 在像你们这样、像我们这样的公司里，需要非常多的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, you need to divide and conquer in any case.
zh: 显然，无论如何你都需要分而治之。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never been a big fan of, I mean, we do value experience, but I think we value experience a lot less than most people.
zh: 我从来都不是……的忠实拥趸，我是说，我们确实重视经验，但我认为我们对经验的重视程度比大多数人低得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe that, yes, being there, done that,
zh: 我相信，是的，经历过、做过，

speaker: Unknown
en: Helps, but there are a few big buts.
zh: 有帮助，但有几个很大的「但是」。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is the world changes pretty fast.
zh: 第一个是，这个世界变化非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm not exactly certain that someone who did something seven years ago, that still applies all that well.
zh: 所以我不太确定某人七年前做过的事情，如今是否还那么适用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there is a huge risk that people will be blind as to the new context because they did it that way and they will just try to paste whatever solution they applied before.
zh: 而且存在一个巨大的风险：人们会对新的环境视而不见，因为他们当年是那么做的，他们会只是试图照搬以前用过的任何解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe you buy some good, but you also buy a lot of bad.
zh: 所以也许你买到了一些好的，但你同时也买到了很多坏的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure which of the two is stronger.
zh: 我不确定两者中哪一个更强。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a company like Benny Spoons,
zh: 对于像 Benny Spoons 这样的公司，

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, we have such a, as far as I can tell, distinctive culture that we found that every time we hired someone, almost every time we hired someone very experienced, they struggled to adapt.
zh: 另外，据我所知，我们有如此独特的文化，我们发现几乎每次我们招一个非常有经验的人，他们都很难适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're so hands-on, no politics, radically candid, everybody needs to...
zh: 我们如此亲力亲为、没有政治、极度坦率，每个人都需要……

speaker: Unknown
en: To carry their own weight.
zh: 承担自己那份重量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it doesn't translate well.
zh: 而这没法很好地迁移过来。

zh: 通常，那些在大型科技公司取得成功的人，他们往往有一种不同的领导风格，这在那些公司里很可能是最优的。

speaker: Unknown

en: So we also need to account for the cost of that cultural change, which sometimes doesn't even happen.
zh: 所以我们还需要把那种文化改变的成本考虑进去，而这种改变有时甚至根本不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it does, it takes a long time.
zh: 即便发生了，也需要很长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And last but not least, I find that generally people lose motivation as they gain experience.
zh: 最后但同样重要的是，我发现通常人们随着经验的增长会失去动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you need to consider whether it's better to have someone with 20 years of experience but, I don't know, 6 out of 10 motivation or someone with 2 years of experience but 10 out of 10 motivation.
zh: 所以你需要考虑，是拥有 20 年经验但动力只有 6/10 的人更好，还是拥有 2 年经验但动力 10/10 的人更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I find often...
zh: 我发现通常……

speaker: Unknown
en: The latter is better.
zh: 后者更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It depends on the situation.
zh: 这取决于情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're generally, we're not big on experience.
zh: 所以总的来说，我们不太看重经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have hired experienced people occasionally, but we prefer to hire.
zh: 我们偶尔也招过有经验的人，但我们更倾向于招……

speaker: Unknown
en: Has that changed as you've scaled?
zh: 随着你们规模化，这一点有变化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you changed your mind at all on that?
zh: 你在这方面改变过想法吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or you're like, actually, no.
zh: 还是说你就是觉得，不，不用改。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, interesting.
zh: 是的，有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, and I may be wrong.
zh: 不，我可能是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, we have tried.
zh: 你看，我们试过。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that we never hired experienced people.
zh: 并不是说我们从不招有经验的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have hired some experienced people with great success.
zh: 我们招过一些有经验的人，而且非常成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that we were completely close-minded regarding that.
zh: 我们在这方面并非完全封闭心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, we keep investing in students or new graduates or people with a couple of years of experience where we think that we can really help them mold their skill set and professional culture in the way that we believe will best
zh: 不，我们持续投资于学生、应届毕业生，或只有几年经验的人，我们认为我们可以真正帮助他们塑造技能组合和职业文化，按照我们相信的、从长远来看最好的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Served them and the company in the long run.
zh: 既服务于他们，也服务于公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also there is a trade-off between talent and experience in a competitive labor market.
zh: 而且在竞争激烈的劳动力市场中，天赋和经验之间存在权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And experience, we can provide it to you.
zh: 经验，我们可以提供给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just need to be a little bit patient.
zh: 我们只需要稍微有点耐心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talent, we can't.
zh: 天赋，我们提供不了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we focus more on talent than experience.
zh: 所以我们更关注天赋而不是经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all considered we're happy with this.
zh: 综合考虑，我们对此很满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: We wouldn't change it necessarily.
zh: 我们不一定非要改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we have encountered
zh: 但我们也遇到过

speaker: Unknown
en: Difficult situations and times where maybe we have a 25-year-old lead engineer showing up at an acquired company and essentially being the person in charge on our end.
zh: 困难的情况和时刻，比如我们一个 25 岁的首席工程师来到一家被收购的公司，实际上成为我们这边的负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people with 20 years of experience thinking, does this guy even know what he's doing?
zh: 而那些有 20 年经验的人会想，这家伙到底知不知道自己在干什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think our track record consistently shows, yeah, it does, or she does, but I can see how it's a more difficult sale than if we had a 50-year-old person with 30 years of experience come in and say the same things.
zh: 而我认为我们的过往记录一直表明，是的，他知道，或者她知道，但我能理解这比派一个 50 岁、有 30 年经验的人来说同样的话要更难让人接受。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's much easier to assume that person is competent, you know?
zh: 人们更容易假设那个人是胜任的，你懂的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've spoken to a couple of the founders of companies you acquired, and one of them said that the person that replaced them was 25, and the other said the person who replaced them was 27.
zh: 我和你们收购的几家公司的创始人聊过，其中一位说接替他的人是 25 岁，另一位说接替他的人是 27 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't seem bothered by it, but I thought that was kind of interesting.
zh: 他们似乎并不介意，但我觉得这挺有意思的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm curious about is like, let's just say that 25-year-old that takes over, I don't know, me or whatever company you're buying,
zh: 我好奇的是，比如说，那个接手的 25 岁年轻人，接手我不知道，我或者你们收购的任何公司，

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you looking for in that person who's going to run that show?
zh: 你在那个要掌控全局的人身上寻找什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a certain quality you're looking for?
zh: 你有在寻找某种特定的特质吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you rotate them around, but let's say it's the first go at it.
zh: 我知道你们会轮换他们，但假设这是第一次做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you looking for?
zh: 你在寻找什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and we wouldn't put someone in that position we haven't tested in a smaller version of it, to be clear.
zh: 是的，需要说明的是，我们不会把一个没有在更小规模上被测试过的人放到那个位置上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's generally someone who led a team or a smaller business before.
zh: 所以通常是一个之前带过团队或更小业务的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yes, it could be someone with just three, four years of experience, a very, very junior.
zh: 但是的，也可能是一个只有三四年经验、非常非常初级的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, on a high level, we look for smart and what we call extreme ownership.
zh: 从高层次上讲，我们寻找的是聪明，以及我们所说的极度主人翁意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being smart for us, I mean, pretty obviously, is you learn very quickly and we have evidence of that.
zh: 聪明，对我们来说，很显然，就是学得非常快，而且我们有证据证明这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're capable, consistently capable of high quality reasoning.
zh: 而且你能够、持续能够进行高质量的推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you propose a solution or you diagnose a problem, consistently what you say or write makes a lot of sense.
zh: 所以当你提出一个解决方案或诊断一个问题时，你所说或所写的一贯都很有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's meaning of all the answers, but your analysis is always rational, accurate, logically sound.
zh: 所有答案都有含义，但你的分析始终是理性的、准确的、逻辑严密的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think that works across the board and in almost any position.
zh: 我们认为这在几乎所有职位上都是通用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, we want you to have extreme ownership, which means you are absolutely
zh: 第二，我们希望你有极度主人翁意识，这意味着你绝对

speaker: Unknown
en: You care tremendously about becoming the best in the world at your job, bringing the greatest possible contribution to your team and the company.
zh: 非常在意在自己的工作中成为世界顶尖，为你的团队和公司带来最大可能的贡献。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're almost fanatical about that.
zh: 你对此几乎近乎狂热。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you find an obstacle or you identify a shortcoming in your skillset, you'll be hell-bent on overcoming that.
zh: 所以当你发现一个障碍，或者识别出自己技能组合中的一个短板时，你会不顾一切地去克服它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then of course we look for more specific skills, but that's really like, we find that that's 80% of the, when those are in place in big ways, those qualities that you're very, very likely to succeed, assuming you're, you know, you can communicate a little bit, you're a nice, you're not an asshole, those, you know, hygienic factors, but the core killer features are those two.
zh: 但当然我们还会看更具体的技能，不过我们发现，当那些素质大体到位时，你非常、非常有可能成功，假设你，你知道，能进行一点沟通，你人不错，你不是个混蛋，这些，你知道，基本卫生因素，但核心的杀手级特质就是那两条。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when it doesn't work, so you put in the 25 year old to run it and like, I don't know, there's an immune system rejection or they just weren't up to it.
zh: 而当它不管用时，比如说你让一个25岁的年轻人去负责，然后，我不知道，出现了免疫系统排异反应，或者他们就是不够格。

speaker: Unknown
en: When is it that falls down?
zh: 什么时候会跌倒呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's happened very rarely.
zh: 这种情况非常罕见。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can only think of one or two cases.
zh: 我只能想起一两个案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when that's happened, I think it's been primarily...
zh: 但当这种情况发生时，我认为主要是……

speaker: Unknown
en: One of two things.
zh: 两种原因之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, the person, while very, very good, because it could also be that we misjudged those qualities, but so far it hasn't been because of any such, we haven't seen any such case, at least for our general managers.
zh: 第一，这个人虽然非常、非常优秀，因为也可能是我们误判了那些素质，但到目前为止还没出现过这种情况，至少对于我们的总经理们，我们没见过这样的案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we've seen is either the person, we basically, we didn't pay enough attention at a person's ability to
zh: 我们见到的是，要么是这个人的，我们基本上，我们没有足够关注一个人的能力，即

speaker: Unknown
en: To lead others, call it communication, a certain level of common sense and empathy.
zh: 去领导他人，可以说是沟通能力，一定程度的常识和同理心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they were incredibly smart problem solvers.
zh: 他们是非常聪明的解决问题的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They moved 100 miles an hour, but they failed to notice when someone was a little bit off, had an issue, they didn't say the right thing at the right time.
zh: 他们以100英里的时速前进，但没能注意到某人有点不对劲、有问题，他们没有在正确的时机说正确的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that basically created a level of hostility or at least friction that ultimately made them untenable as leaders.
zh: 这基本上造成了一种敌意，或至少是摩擦，最终使他们作为领导者难以为继。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other case was where enough people in the org, for all sorts of reasons, felt more competent.
zh: 另一种情况是，组织里有足够多的人，出于各种原因，觉得自己更有能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And although this person was great and super nice and empathetic and communicative, these people couldn't get over the fact that, oh, I'm so much more experienced, I cannot be led by this person, even if just formally.
zh: 尽管这个人很棒、非常友善、有同理心、善于沟通，这些人就是无法接受，哦，我经验丰富得多，我不能被这个人领导，哪怕只是名义上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's been very rare, but I can remember one such case where that occurred.
zh: 这种情况非常罕见，但我能记得发生过这么一个案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And look, and there we could do one of two things.
zh: 你看，当时我们可以做两件事之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: We either move or part ways with these people who reject leadership or we change the leader.
zh: 我们要么调动或与这些拒绝领导的人分道扬镳，要么更换领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it depends on the context of which of the two makes more sense.
zh: 这取决于具体情境，哪一种更合理。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you develop these people?
zh: 你如何培养这些人？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, do you actually train them, develop them, coach them?
zh: 比如，你真的会培训他们、培养他们、指导他们吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or it's like they're smart, they're going to figure it out.
zh: 还是说他们很聪明，他们会自己搞明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: You kind of throw them into it and they're good.
zh: 你把他们扔进去，他们就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we have training materials, but broadly, I think 90% of the outcome depends on you throw them into the deep end of the pool.
zh: 是的，我们有培训材料，但总的来说，我认为90%的结果取决于你把他们扔进泳池的深水区。

speaker: Unknown
en: You give them way more responsibility that seems reasonable.
zh: 你给他们的责任感远超看似合理的程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you surround them with amazing colleagues.
zh: 然后你让他们身边围绕出色的同事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We find that we learn primarily by working with amazing people.
zh: 我们发现，我们主要通过和出色的人一起工作来学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost invariably, some of the people around you will be better than you at some things.
zh: 几乎毫无例外，你周围的某些人在某些方面会比你强。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you try to emulate those good traits, you'll learn from those.
zh: 所以如果你试图模仿那些好的特质，你会从中学到东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, you know, they will suck at some things.
zh: 而且，你知道，他们也会在某些方面很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you notice the weaknesses, you can avoid falling into the same trap yourself.
zh: 如果你注意到那些弱点，你就能避免自己掉进同样的坑。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the level of responsibility and the level of talent around you are the two things that we find drive growth the most.
zh: 所以责任感程度和你身边人才的水平，是我们发现最能驱动成长的两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I mean, a little bit of formal training here and there and active coaching certainly adds that 10, 20% extra for sure.
zh: 不过，是的，这里一点正式培训、那里一些积极指导，确实会带来那额外的10%、20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I tell you the one thing that helped me on my journey?
zh: 我能告诉你一件在我成长路上帮到我的事吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We decided we're going to do a 360 degree review for me, which was a good idea.
zh: 我们决定为我做一次360度评估，这是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my co-founder volunteered, which is a strange thing because he's really introverted.
zh: 我的联合创始人自告奋勇，这很奇怪，因为他真的很内向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, how do I do this without talking to other homo sapiens?
zh: 他就像，我要怎么在不和其他智人交谈的情况下做这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he did a net promoter survey.
zh: 于是他做了一次净推荐值调查。

speaker: Unknown
en: First question is, on a scale of one to 10, I'd like you to recommend Brian as the CEO of HubSpot.
zh: 第一个问题是，在1到10的量表上，我希望你推荐Brian担任HubSpot的CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And number two is, why did you give that number?
zh: 第二个问题是，你为什么给这个分数？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then send it out to like 25 people, the board, customers, employees.
zh: 然后把它发给大约25个人，董事会、客户、员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like people wrote frigging novels.
zh: 人们简直写出了长篇大论。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, they wrote long novels.
zh: 我是说，他们写了很长的长篇大论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he spent some time, correlated it, showed me the histogram, very helpful.
zh: 他花了一些时间，做了关联分析，给我看了直方图，非常有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he did something clever, like for each feature, be like, here's a feature.
zh: 然后他做了件聪明的事，比如对每一个特质，就像，这是一个特质。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he would pull out direct quotes on what people said about the feature.
zh: 他会抽出人们关于该特质的直接引述。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it really hit home to me that, okay, that's a feature.
zh: 所以这真的让我深刻意识到，好吧，那是一个特质。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the first 10 pages, I'm going through the report and I'm like, feature, feature, I got this.
zh: 在报告的前10页里，我边看边想，特质、特质，这个我拿下了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am fantastic at the COP.
zh: 我在COP上表现极其出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have this absolutely nailed.
zh: 这个我绝对稳了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Page 11 is where the bug started.
zh: 第 11 页就是 bug 开始的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then- Ooh!
zh: 然后—— 哦！

speaker: Unknown
en: That's painful.
zh: 那很痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the direct quotes in there, it was incredibly helpful to help me get better.
zh: 里面的直接引用，对帮助我进步非常有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my ahas, by the way, was some of the features were bugs.
zh: 顺便说一句，我的一个领悟是，有些功能其实是 bug。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, people didn't like that.
zh: 你知道，人们不喜欢那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was really passionate, and sometimes I get really excited about things.
zh: 我当时非常有热情，有时候我对事情会感到非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the first year, I tried to fix all my bugs.
zh: 所以第一年，我试着修复我所有的 bug。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then second, third, fourth year, I'm like, I'm gonna pick one or two of the bugs I'm gonna work on.
zh: 然后第二、第三、第四年，我就想，我要挑一两个我要解决的 bug。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you personally go about getting feedback and getting better, and how do you do that with your folks?
zh: 你个人是怎么获取反馈并变得更好的，你又是怎么和你的团队一起做的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we're big on feedback, a bit like you just described.
zh: 是的，我们非常重视反馈，就像你刚才描述的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have something called radical candor internally.
zh: 我们内部有一种叫「绝对坦率」的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, the idea is you should always tell people when you see something good or bad, as long as you don't share that because you're venting or because you believe there's a chance that they could improve or the team could benefit or the company could benefit, you should share.
zh: 基本上，这个理念是，当你看到好的或坏的事情时，你应该始终告诉别人，只要你说出来不是因为你在发泄，而是因为你相信他们有改进的机会，或者团队或公司能从中受益，你就应该说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't worry about the accuracy of what you're saying, the wording, whether you hurt feelings.
zh: 别担心你说的话是否准确、措辞如何、是否会伤害感情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, try to be nice if you can, but that's secondary to being honest.
zh: 当然，如果可以的话尽量友善，但那是次要的，诚实才是首要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, of course, we're not perfect.
zh: 所以，当然，我们并不完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everybody does it all the time, but we try to have this
zh: 不是每个人都时时刻刻都这样做，但我们努力营造这样一种

speaker: Unknown
en: environment where opinions and observations flow very quickly and abundantly.
zh: 环境：观点和观察可以非常快速且大量地流动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's a very good source of learning.
zh: 所以这是一个非常好的学习来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: You make everyone do it face-to-face.
zh: 你让每个人都面对面地做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we try, but our recommendation is to, if it happens in person, say it immediately, even in front of everybody in a meeting.
zh: 是的，我们努力这样做，但我们的建议是，如果是当面发生的，就立刻说出来，即使在会议上当着所有人的面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't delay, just say it.
zh: 不要拖延，直接说出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, respectfully and pathetically, but just straight up.
zh: 当然，要尊重且有同理心，但就是直截了当。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's something that you notice through asynchronous communications, such as on Slack, then you can send them a message or whatever.

speaker: Unknown
en: Rather than more is a very, very useful thing, even in this day and age, particularly because I think the fact that some of these companies are pulling it off, it doesn't mean that they've chosen the right path.
zh: 而不是更多是一件非常有用的事情，即使在今天这个时代，尤其是因为我认为这些公司做成了一些事，并不意味着它们选对了路。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know how well they would have done had they done three rather than four things and dropping the smallest, least important one.
zh: 我们不知道如果它们做三件事而不是四件事、砍掉最小最不重要的那件事，会做得怎么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe the biggest, most important one would have been 35% better and bigger and maybe it's a net positive.
zh: 也许最大最重要那件事会好 35%、大 35%，也许净结果是正的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're big on, we have a value actually or a quality that we call relentless simplification.
zh: 你知道，我们非常重视，我们实际上有一个我们称之为「不懈简化」的价值观或品质。

speaker: Unknown
en: We measure ourselves against and we demand.
zh: 我们以此衡量自己，并且我们要求如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you measure yourself?
zh: 你怎么衡量自己？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's fascinating.
zh: 这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, measure, I meant like we, yeah, we assess ourselves against.
zh: 是的，衡量，我是说我们，是的，我们以此评估自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not, frankly, it's not very, very quantifiable, but we want people to, every time, so the rule goes like this.
zh: 说实话，它不是非常非常可量化的，但我们希望人们，每一次，规则是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time someone recommends that we should add complexity, whether it's a step in a process, a feature,
zh: 每当有人建议我们应该增加复杂性，无论是流程中的一个步骤、一个功能、

speaker: Unknown
en: A team, headcount to a team, you name it, any element of the system, the burden of proof is on those making that recommendation.
zh: 一个团队、一个团队的人头数，随便什么，系统的任何元素，举证责任都在提出建议的人身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those who believe it's a bad idea don't need to bother bringing any proof.
zh: 那些认为这是个坏主意的人不需要费心拿出任何证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're fine.
zh: 他们没事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if we choose to go forward, there needs to be very clear proof that it makes sense or it has to be revertible and the people who...
zh: 所以如果我们选择继续推进，就需要非常明确的证据证明它合理，或者它必须是可回退的，而那些……

speaker: Unknown
en: Drive the initiative need to then determine whether it was a clear success and otherwise revert it pretty quickly.
zh: 推动这个举措的人需要随后判断它是否是明确的成功，否则要很快回退它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other part of the rule is that we need to stay alert and question complexity that's been there for a while, because we become blind to it as human beings.
zh: 规则的另一部分是，我们需要保持警觉，质疑那些存在了一段时间的复杂性，因为作为人类，我们会对此变得盲目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And anyone who does that should always be applauded, even if it's a nuisance that, oh my goodness, again, we're questioning this process or this policy.
zh: 而任何这样做的人都应该总是受到赞扬，即使这是一种讨人嫌的行为，「天哪，又来了，我们又在质疑这个流程或这个政策」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, if you have better technology, AI is amazing.
zh: 是的，如果你有更好的技术，AI 是了不起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, as someone who failed with AI startup in 2010, I mean, I didn't fail 2010.
zh: 你知道，作为一个在 2010 年做过 AI 创业公司并失败的人，我是说，我不是 2010 年失败的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started in 2010, failed in 2013.
zh: 我们 2010 年开始，2013 年失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly, I believe in the power of technology.
zh: 显然，我相信技术的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not surprised we can do a lot more today than we could 20 years ago.
zh: 我不惊讶我们今天能比 20 年前做得多得多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You decided to base a company in Milan.
zh: 你决定把公司设在米兰。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were based in Boston.
zh: 我们当时在波士顿。

speaker: Unknown
en: I felt like there were some big pluses and big minuses to being in Boston.
zh: 我觉得在波士顿有一些很大的好处和一些很大的坏处。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people think just you can't create a great company out of Silicon Valley.
zh: 很多人认为除了硅谷之外你根本没法创建一家伟大的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's obviously not me.
zh: 那显然不是我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why didn't you do Milan?
zh: 你为什么不选米兰？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the pluses and minuses of building outside the valley?
zh: 在硅谷之外创业的好处和坏处是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you permanently feel like you're not a cool kid because you're in Milan?
zh: 你会不会永远觉得自己因为身在米兰而不是酷孩子？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I actually couldn't care less about coolness.
zh: 你知道吗，我其实根本不在乎酷不酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone who buys a company like AOL cannot possibly care about coolness.
zh: 一个买下 AOL 这种公司的人，不可能在乎酷不酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: If anything, or maybe I do care, but I think that the uncool is cool.
zh: 如果说我在乎，或者也许我真的在乎，但我觉得不酷才是酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: You choose, but it's one or the other.
zh: 你自己选吧，反正二者必居其一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not certain.
zh: 我不确定。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the pluses or what are the minuses?
zh: 好处是什么，坏处又是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: My thesis is San Francisco is the best place in the world to start a company, but holy crap is it hard to scale there.
zh: 我的论点是，旧金山是世界上最适合创办公司的地方，但要命的是，在那里扩张实在太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so expensive that there's not a lot of loyalty.
zh: 那里太贵了，没什么忠诚度可言。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just darn hard to scale.
zh: 扩张就是 darn 难。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your thesis on it?
zh: 你对这件事的论点是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, look, I haven't built a company in San Francisco, so I can't really tell for sure.
zh: 是这样的，你看，我没在旧金山创办过公司，所以我不能百分百确定。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does strike me as a place.
zh: 但它确实给我一种印象。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have the coolest, highest potential, best resourced company on the planet, I think that's where we want to build it.
zh: 如果你拥有这颗星球上最酷、潜力最高、资源最好的公司，我想那就是你想把它建起来的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can probably absorb the most talent, the fastest there than anywhere else.
zh: 在那里，你吸收人才的速度可能是最快的，比其他任何地方都快。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are more of a middling project,
zh: 而如果你是一个比较中不溜的项目，

zh: 顺便说一句，按硅谷标准来看，中不溜已经是相当高的门槛了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it may be harder there than in many other locations.
zh: 那么在那里可能就比在其他许多地方更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: In any case, we chose Italy, Milan.
zh: 不管怎样，我们选择了意大利，米兰。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today we're an international company.
zh: 如今我们是一家国际化公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're hiring way more people outside of Italy than in Italy at this point.
zh: 到这个阶段，我们在意大利以外招的人远远多于在意大利招的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, including now more and more in the States, I think we'll probably open offices there in the next year.
zh: 不过，你知道，包括现在在美国也越来越多，我想我们明年可能会在那里开设办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, we started it in Milan, Italy.
zh: 是的，我们在意大利米兰起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: On purpose, we actually were in Denmark with my co-founders where we had completed our engineering studies and had launched and then shut down our AI startup.
zh: 这是刻意的，其实当时我和我的联合创始人在丹麦，我们在那里完成了工程学的学业，并且创办过又关掉了一家 AI 创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had two main reasons.
zh: 我们主要有两个理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was...
zh: 第一个是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Extremely, you know, commercial and selfish.
zh: 非常，你知道，商业化和自私的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically what you described, we thought Italy, 60 million people, excellent education, relatively few amazing companies, certainly very few, if any, up-and-coming tech companies could be a win-win for us in the talent.
zh: 基本上就是你描述的那样，我们想，意大利有六千万人，教育优秀，但了不起的公司相对很少，能称得上崛起中的科技公司更是寥寥无几甚至没有，这对我们的人才策略来说可能是双赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we brought a lot of ambition.
zh: 比如说，我们带来了很多雄心壮志。

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought an idea that made a lot of sense, a project that we thought was exciting.
zh: 我们觉得有一个很有道理的想法，一个我们觉得很令人兴奋的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of people would otherwise be relegated to joining a
zh: 这样一来，很多原本只能屈就加入一家

speaker: Unknown
en: Inferior business or moving abroad, but they had their family there, they loved it there, could actually stay and have everything, both an exciting job and stay with their families.
zh: 较差的公司、或者只能移居国外的人——但他们家人都在那里，他们热爱那里——就可以留下来，鱼与熊掌兼得，既有一份令人兴奋的工作，又能和家人在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we thought we'd be able to build a better team basically for the same dollars or an equally good team for cheaper, which I think has proven to be true and a significant advantage.
zh: 于是我们想，基本上我们能够用同样的钱打造一支更好的团队，或者用更少的钱打造一支同样好的团队，我认为这一点已经被证明是事实，而且是一大优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other reason was more missionary.
zh: 另一个理由则更多是出于使命感。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believed, and I think my co-founders
zh: 我相信，我想我的联合创始人

speaker: Unknown
en: did too and we certainly believe so today that the world in general is a better place if
zh: 也一样，而且我们今天当然仍然坚信，如果

speaker: Unknown
en: Knowledge, opportunity, wealth are a little bit better distributed.
zh: 知识、机会、财富能被更均匀地分配一些，这个世界总体上会是一个更好的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's totally fine and probably even a good thing that you have one or two hubs like Silicon Valley that are one notch above.
zh: 我觉得有一两个像硅谷这样高出一等的中心，完全没问题，甚至可能是件好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the world probably needs that to achieve maximum prosperity.
zh: 我想这个世界大概需要这样，才能实现最大程度的繁荣。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think if the gap becomes immense and basically everything that matters happens in one or two places, it's a really big problem, including for the people who live in those places in the long run.
zh: 但我认为，如果差距变得巨大，基本上所有重要的事情都发生在一两个地方，那就是一个非常严重的问题，长远来看，对生活在那些地方的人也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we wanted to
zh: 所以我们想做

speaker: Unknown
en: Do our part.
zh: 我们自己的一份贡献。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make a 1% change by showing you can build a world-beating company with massive ambitions in an unlikely place, Italy being one of many, clearly.
zh: 做出 1% 的改变，证明你可以在一个看似不可能的地方打造一家拥有远大抱负的世界级公司——意大利显然只是诸多这样的地方之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we are Italian.
zh: 但我们是意大利人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was easy.
zh: 这很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: We understood the culture better.
zh: 我们更了解那里的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we don't regret it.
zh: 我们不后悔。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was a good move.
zh: 我认为那是一步好棋。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can never A-B test life.
zh: 人生没办法做 A/B 测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I cannot definitively say that we would have done less well had we started in Silicon Valley.
zh: 所以我无法斩钉截铁地说，如果我们当初在硅谷起步，就会做得更差。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do suspect that this has been a better choice for us.
zh: 但我确实怀疑这对我们来说是一个更好的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: My last question, so I interviewed three of the founders, didn't interview, I called three of the founders of companies you acquired.
zh: 我的最后一个问题，我采访了三位创始人，不是采访，是打电话给三位被你收购的公司的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all three of them said the same thing.
zh: 他们三个都说了同样的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: They said, you are exceptionally high integrity.
zh: 他们说，你有着 exceptionally 高的诚信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't hear that a lot about CEOs necessarily.
zh: 关于 CEO，我不常听到这样的评价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't hear that a lot in preparation for these calls.
zh: 在为这些通话做准备时，我也不常听到这样的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there some principles around that you live by?
zh: 你有什么关于这方面的原则吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what are they?
zh: 它们是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what can we borrow from you?
zh: 我们能从你身上借鉴什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know that, you know, it's up to you to determine whether it's worth borrowing, but it's not a point of expedience, it's a moral point, so that morality is very personal.
zh: 我不知道，你知道，是否值得借鉴由你来判断，但这不是一个权宜之计的问题，这是一个道德问题，所以道德是非常个人化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point early in my adult life, I decided that I never
zh: 在我成年生活的早期某个时候，我决定我永远

en: So, I mean, I can be transparent about it.
zh: 所以，我的意思是，我可以对此保持透明。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not...
zh: 这不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: So, in my early 20s, I cheated on my girlfriend at the time.
zh: 在我二十岁出头的时候，我背叛了当时的女友。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was so ashamed.
zh: 我感到非常羞愧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes I think making a big mistake...
zh: 有时我觉得犯一个大错……

speaker: Unknown
en: is a better way of learning than rationalizing how you should conduct yourself.
zh: 是比为自己该如何行事找合理化理由更好的学习方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was so ashamed of myself that I made a promise to myself to never lie but also never omit something important that people should know, even if it's to my detriment.
zh: 我对自己感到如此羞愧，以至于我对自己许下承诺：永远不说谎，但也永远不隐瞒人们应该知道的重要事情，即使这对我自己不利。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've tried to extend that to all aspects of my life.
zh: 所以我试着把这一点延伸到我生活的所有方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I suspect that although it's sometimes costly in the short run,
zh: 我怀疑，虽然这在短期内有时代价高昂，

speaker: Unknown
en: It tends to pay off in the long run.
zh: 但它往往在长期会有回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm very glad.
zh: 我非常高兴。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just made my day sharing that feedback.
zh: 你分享这个反馈让我今天很开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't know you talked to them.
zh: 我不知道你和他们谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm glad you did, and I'm glad they said that over praising my looks or something.
zh: 但我很高兴你这么做了，我很高兴他们这么说，而不是夸我的外貌什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, because it really matters.
zh: 不，因为这真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, jokes aside, it really matters to me.
zh: 不，玩笑 aside，这对我真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a life mission I set on for myself to be that kind of person you can trust is telling you things as they are, at least as I think they are.
zh: 成为一个你可以信任的人、告诉你事情真实面貌的人——至少按我认为的真实面貌——这是我为我自己设定的人生使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it does pay off in the long run when you become known as someone who can be trusted.
zh: 是的，我认为从长期来看这确实有回报，当你成为众所周知可以信任的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easier to have a good life, make good friends and relationships that last that matter, do business.
zh: 拥有美好的生活、结交持久的、有意义的好朋友和关系、做生意，都会更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: People will come to you and say, okay, we're looking to sell.
zh: 人们会来找你说，好，我们正在考虑出售。

speaker: Unknown
en: We believe you guys.
zh: 我们相信你们。 [[752-782]] 你们的承诺是有分量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your word means something.
zh: 你们的承诺是有分量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it doesn't come from a place of seeking expedience.
zh: 但这并不是出于追求权宜之计。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really just a moral point for me.
zh: 这对我来说真的只是一个道德问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's very subjective in that regard.
zh: 在这个意义上，它是非常主观的。

en: I love that.
zh: 我很喜欢这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to leave it there.
zh: 我就问到这里。

en: Congratulations on building something really special.
zh: 祝贺你建立了一些真正特别的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good luck to you on your journey to a trillion dollars, my friend.
zh: 祝你在一万亿美元之旅上好运，我的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll do our best.
zh: 我们会尽最大努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a pleasure.
zh: 这是一次愉快的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for having me, Brian.
zh: 谢谢你邀请我，Brian。

speaker: Unknown
en: Appreciate it.
zh: 很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

en: I thought Luca was really interesting.
zh: 我觉得 Luca 真的很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: His company is doing really well.
zh: 他的公司做得真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the guy beats to his own drummer.
zh: 这个人自成一派。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to stick on the ending there.
zh: 就停留在这个结尾吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, for CEOs, integrity is really an underrated thing.
zh: 我是说,对于 CEO 来说,正直真的是一件被低估的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are what your word is.
zh: 你的话就是你这个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got a great reputation probably, but you do one stupid thing and you can kind of have that crash down.
zh: 你可能有很好的声誉,但只要你做一件蠢事,那声誉就可能崩塌。

en: So I like that.
zh: 所以我很喜欢这一点。

en: I like that he's like, I never lie.

en: And I never omit important info.

en: But I had three of the companies he acquired kind of say the same thing.

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, if you're never going to omit important information when talking to someone, you're going to have conflict.
zh: 等等,其他我觉得很独特的事情,比如他招人的方式在很多不同层面上都很独特。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that just sort of reinforces that in my mind.
